objective: Confirmatory Monte Carlo of not-all-equal's emergence and the cyclic-edge topology on twisted square-lattice tori: aspect ratios, both odd-side patterns, sheared and rotated tori, long cylinders. Pre-registered tests: the exact reduction and duality as controls; scale-free emergence; rotation invariance; rejection of the Pinson-Arguin Coulomb-gas family; the candidate exact value of one half bit on square tori with one odd side; the candidate long-cylinder exponent 1/16; the bulk class against published strongly-connected percolation values (fractal dimension, untwisted wrapping probabilities); the two-way arm exponent against 5/24.
status: Closed: supported by NAE-INVARIANT-20261022-001B-E001 (confirmatory Monte Carlo, frozen contract, 54 rows, 2136 s; controls pass: the strong-component and odd-cluster tests agree on every sample, contractible and cross counts agree on every twisted torus, bipartite tori always consistent; independent replay agrees). Emergence is scale-free on every shape within 3 sigma + 0.02 bits: 0.846 (square, both sides odd), 1.033 (5:3), 1.751 (3:1), 0.497 pair average (square, one odd side), 1.164 and 0.125 (2:1 with the odd side short or long), 2.339 and 0.010 (4:1), 0.653 (sheared squares), 0.834-0.839 (rotated squares, same as the axis square). The Pinson-Arguin Coulomb-gas family is rejected (chi-square 1330 per degree of freedom). The bulk is the strongly-connected percolation class: fractal dimension 1.798-1.815, untwisted wrapping 0.8617/0.7498/0.6379 against 0.8612/0.7500/0.6387 published, one-way arms 5/48, two-way arms 0.1969 (not 5/24; equal to beta/nu). Candidates: half a bit on square tori with one odd side accepted (E_inf 0.4993 +- 0.0011); the long-cylinder exponent 0.0645 +- 0.0003 rejects 1/16.
title: Experiment: the shape scan and the identification tests
